dedupe_keys.name: hurricane sandy flooding of lower manhattan data centres and the 75 broad street fuel brigade 2012

description: This emergency-response case describes what happened to data centres in Lower Manhattan when Hurricane Sandy's storm surge flooded the district on 29 and 30 October 2012. At 75 Broad Street, a high-rise used by colocation providers including Peer 1 Hosting and Internap, salt water filled the basement and stood four feet deep in the lobby, destroying the fuel pumps and the tenants' basement fuel tanks, so diesel generators stopped and most tenants had to shut down. Peer 1's generator on the 17th floor roof still worked, and for about two days staff and customers, including the founder of Squarespace, carried diesel in five-gallon buckets up 17 flights of stairs to keep it running until fuel could be pumped. Other facilities nearby, such as 33 Whitehall Street and 111 Eighth Avenue, also had flooding or fuel problems, and many websites went offline. Coverage: data centres in Lower Manhattan, 29 October to early November 2012. Format and access: free trade-press reports and an Availability Digest summary. Caveats: accounts are anecdotal and operator-led; no official inquiry into data centres was made. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of basement fuel and electrical plant to coastal flooding, emergency response and fuel logistics for long grid outages, and design retrofits that move plant above flood level. Related records: the FCC 2017 hurricane season and Katrina panel cases cover telecom networks, and XDI's climate-risk analysis ranks flood exposure of data-centre hubs.
